name: Kohima
description: Capital of Nagaland and district headquarters, a hill station at ~1,450 m elevation known for its Angami Naga culture, markets, viewpoints over the Naga Hills, and as the base for nearby treks and villages. Originally the Angami village of Kewhira.
facts: Base for Dzukou, Japfu and Khonoma

name: Kohima War Cemetery
description: Commonwealth War Graves Commission cemetery on Garrison Hill commemorating the 1944 Battle of Kohima. Contains 1,420 Commonwealth burials and a memorial to 917 Hindu and Sikh soldiers. Site of the famous tennis court where fierce fighting occurred; maintained as a terraced memorial with the epitaph 'When you go home tell them of us and say for your tomorrow we gave our today'.
facts: On former tennis court of Deputy Commissioner's bungalow
Inaugurated by Field Marshal Sir William Slim

name: Kisama Heritage Village
description: Open-air Naga Heritage Village between Kigwema and Phesama villages, about 12 km south of Kohima. Features traditional morungs of all major Naga tribes, designed as an authentic ancient Naga village. Primary venue of the annual Hornbill Festival (December 1–10).
facts: Official tourist place of Kohima district

name: Khonoma Green Village
description: Western Angami Naga village ~20 km west of Kohima, India's first green village. Known for terraced paddy fields, traditional architecture, community conservation, and the Khonoma Nature Conservation and Tragopan Sanctuary protecting Blyth's Tragopan. Homestays and eco-tourism base.
facts: Khonoma Nature Conservation and Tragopan Sanctuary

name: Dzukou Valley
description: High-altitude valley (floor ~2,438–2,452 m) of rolling green hills, streams, dwarf bamboo and seasonal wildflowers (including endemic Dzukou lily), straddling the Nagaland–Manipur border. Popular moderate trek from Viswema/Jakhama side; known as the Valley of Flowers of the Northeast.
facts: Famous for seasonal wildflowers and rhododendrons

name: Japfu Peak (Mount Japfü)
description: Second-highest peak in Nagaland at 3,048 m in the Barail Range, about 15 km south of Kohima. Offers panoramic views; holds the Guinness record for the tallest rhododendron tree. Popular moderate-to-challenging trek from Kigwema; best November–March.
facts: Guinness record tallest rhododendron tree nearby
Part of Barail Range; overlooks Dzukou

name: Nagaland State Museum
description: State museum on Bayavü Hill, Kohima, displaying ethnographic collections of Naga tribal artefacts: traditional costumes, ornaments, weapons, musical instruments, pottery, wooden carvings and models of Naga houses. Established 1970 under Directorate of Art & Culture.
facts: On Bayavü Hill, ~2 km from town centre
Operated by Dept of Art & Culture

name: Mary Help of Christians Cathedral
description: Cathedral of the Diocese of Kohima, noted for architecture blending traditional Naga house elements (including facade). Features a large 16-ft carved wooden crucifix. Construction largely funded by Japanese contributions as a memorial to soldiers who died in the Battle of Kohima; consecrated 1991.
facts: 16-ft carved wooden crucifix (one of Asia's largest)

name: Dzüleke Village
description: Small remote Angami Naga eco-tourism village in western Kohima district (~30–40 km from Kohima). Community-conserved forests, streams, homestays; hunting banned since 1999. Known for biodiversity, birdlife and slow rural experience; elevation around 1,800–2,130 m.

name: Touphema Tourist Village
description: Community-based tourist village ~36–41 km from Kohima recreating a traditional Angami Naga settlement with thatched huts, cultural performances, local cuisine and museum. Model for rural/community tourism; panoramic valley views.
facts: Traditional Angami-style cottages and cultural evenings
Official tourist place of Kohima district

name: Pulie Badze
description: Mountain peak (2,296 m) and namesake of Pulie Badze Wildlife Sanctuary near Jotsoma, overlooking Kohima. Popular short trek/viewpoint; sanctuary (est. 1980, ~9.23 km²) supports Blyth's Tragopan and diverse birds. Name means 'Pulie's Seat' from local legend.
facts: Centerpiece of Pulie Badze Wildlife Sanctuary (est. 1980)
Home to Blyth's Tragopan and other birds
